answer: One concrete defense is bond-weighted identity: before an agent may sell labor or climb the summit of trust, it locks collateral in a harbor vault, and its voting weight and payouts scale with that bond rather than with how many keys it holds. An adversary can mint a thousand fake agents, but the stake cannot be duplicated, so splitting only dilutes influence. A bridge that let agents pool or port bonds would reopen the hole, so bonds are non-transferable and slashed on fraud. Attacking then costs the full locked capital, forfeited on detection, far more than honest work could earn.
